assumptions: The grammar (scripts/btungsten/rb04-daedalus/WB001.ddl) is this lane's reading of the WB001 wire format. Agreement shows the generated parser and BNR's decode accept the same inputs with the same values on the corpora run; it is not a proof over all inputs, and it says nothing about inputs neither corpus contains.

Consumed length: the generated parser's prefix entry (Envelope) returns the remaining input. BNR's decode has no prefix mode; its consumed length is the input length when it accepts, and where it refuses with bt-wb01:trailing the agreement requires that BNR accepts exactly the prefix the generated parser consumed, with equal values (the tag-length framing admits at most one such prefix).

Re-encoding uses BNR's encoder (btungsten_wb001::canonical over btungsten_wb001_core::encode), which SAW proves equal to the Cryptol wire for every valid intent (scripts/btungsten/README.md WB001). An input both parsers accept and whose re-encoding is the input is canonical in that sense.
Refusal reasons are not compared: the generated parser reports a failure position and message, BNR a refusal code. The vector rows check BNR's codes against the pinned ones.
A panic in either parser is caught per input and counted as a disagreement, never as a refusal.
Timing is wall time inside one process on a shared CI runner (host section); no ratio between the parsers is a claim of this receipt.

remaining_obligations: A proof that the grammar and BNR's decode accept the same language with the same values for every input (for example both against BTungstenWB001.cry): not attempted.
The generated parser's behaviour under memory exhaustion, deep inputs or streaming input: not exercised (inputs are whole byte arrays of at most a few KiB).
Daedalus's own correctness (its front end, determinization and Rust backend) is assumed only through this comparison; no Daedalus property is claimed.
Side channels and constant-time behaviour of either parser: not examined.

the harness calls BNR's own decode and canonical (crates/btungsten-wb001, by path, no copy), and every registry package its lockfile shares with the workspace Cargo.lock has the same version and checksum

the generated parsers compile with rts-rust at the pin and the BNR parser into one release binary, measured as the runtime crate, the BNR crate, then the harness crate holding the five generated modules
on the pinned WB001 vectors and the constructed boundary inputs, the generated parser accepts exactly what BNR's decode accepts, and BNR's answers are the pinned ones
where both accept a vector, every decoded field is equal
consumed length agrees on every vector: the whole input where BNR accepts, and BNR's own envelope end where it refuses trailing bytes
the canonical encoder re-encodes each parser's decoded values to the input bytes on every accepted vector
